name: Synchral
description: Synchral is a targeted cross-modal neural disruptor that temporarily dissolves the boundaries between sensory processing regions, inducing full-spectrum synesthesia. Sound becomes visible as flowing chromatic structures, color emits audible tones, and touch produces smell and taste responses. Helix designed it as a therapeutic tool for sensory rehabilitation but it escaped into the recreational market within months of its first clinical trial.
effects: Full cross-modal synesthesia — all senses bleed into each other
Profound sense of sensory unity and interconnectedness
Music becomes a visual-tactile-olfactory experience simultaneously
Emotional states acquire physical textures and colors
Strong feelings of cosmic interconnection and meaning
side_effects: Disorientation and inability to navigate physical space during peak
Nausea if exposed to discordant or aggressive sounds
Rare cases of synesthetic binding — cross-wiring persists after drug wears off (weeks to permanent)
BCI users may experience involuntary data-feed integration into sensory experience
cultural_context: Synchral gave birth to an entire genre of GLMZ music called Bleed — compositions designed specifically to be experienced on the drug, with frequencies and rhythms calibrated to produce specific visual and tactile phenomena. Bleed concerts are semi-legal events in Tier 2-3 underground venues. Among BCI-heavy communities, Synchral is controversial — the interaction between the drug and neural interfaces is unpredictable and has caused several cases of permanent sensory cross-wiring.
story_hooks: A Bleed musician has discovered that specific Synchral-activated sound frequencies can embed subliminal commands in BCI users — and someone has been funding her tours specifically to exploit this

A black-market Synchral batch has been causing permanent synesthetic binding in one in twenty users — the street chemist who modified the formula has gone missing and the affected users are organizing
A Tier 5 collector is paying extreme prices for art created by Synchral-bound artists — people whose synesthesia never faded — claiming their work accesses something no sober artist can reach
